vulnerability.title: Axios: CRLF Injection in multipart/form-data body via unsanitized blob.type in formDataToStream
vulnerability.category_l2: CRLF sequences in an attacker-controlled Blob/File .type are interpolated into a multipart part's Content-Type header, injecting per-part headers into the form-data body

severity.source: GitHub (CNA GitHub_M) CVSS 3.1 5.3 MEDIUM; NVD vulnStatus Analyzed with the same 5.3 MEDIUM as a Secondary metric from security-advisories@github.com; OSV GHSA database_specific severity MODERATE with the same CVSS_V3 vector; CISA-ADP SSVC records Exploitation poc, Automatable no, Technical Impact partial

fixed_releases.verified_content: Tag v1.15.1 peels to ac42446be51300fe214ba3c6e40cc95f34fd6871; its lib/helpers/formDataToStream.js blob 76127910 equals the post-fix blob of commit 7587327 and contains the CR/LF-stripping construction at lines 27-28. The npm 1.15.1 tarball's package/lib/helpers/formDataToStream.js has sha256 9412131c..., byte-identical to the tag file.

vulnerability.vulnerable_commit_basis: tag v1.15.0 peels to 772a4e54, inside the advisory range >=1.0.0,<1.15.1; its lib/helpers/formDataToStream.js blob f191e8cb interpolates value.type into the Content-Type line (line 27) without removing CR/LF, while the string branch at line 25 replaces CR/LF and escapeName at lines 54-62 percent-encodes them for name and filename.

location.verification_method: Static read of lib/helpers/formDataToStream.js at tag v1.15.0 and v1.15.1, the fix commit 7587327 patch against its parent, git object identity checks, npm 1.15.0/1.15.1 tarball file comparison, and the saved OSV/CVE/NVD records. No JavaScript was executed and no HTTP request was made by this collector.

critical_operation.description: The constructor builds the per-part headers of a multipart body. name and filename pass through escapeName, which percent-encodes CR, LF and double quote, and the string-value branch replaces CR/LF sequences. The Blob/File branch instead interpolates value.type verbatim at line 27, so an attacker-controlled type such as 'image/jpeg\r\nX-Injected: 1' terminates the Content-Type header and starts an injected header line inside the part. Line 30 encodes the assembled headers and FormDataPart.encode yields them as the part prefix, so the injected bytes reach the wire inside the multipart body. The fix at 7587327 assigns String(value.type || 'application/octet-stream').replace(/[\r\n]/g, '') to safeType before interpolation.

entry_point.description: In the Node.js adapter, when utils.isSpecCompliantForm(data) is true the adapter calls formDataToStream(data, headersHandler, {tag, boundary}) at line 512, forwarding the caller-supplied FormData entries to the vulnerable constructor. Reachable through the public axios.post(url, formData) API with no special configuration.

source_crosscheck.notes: Severity is consistent: the CNA, OSV and the NVD Secondary metric all give CVSS 3.1 5.3 MEDIUM with the same vector, and OSV's MODERATE is GitHub's qualitative label for that score; no contradictory metric exists. CWE-93 is identical across all three records. The affected range >=1.0.0,<1.15.1 agrees between the CNA, OSV and NVD CPE data. Source independence is weak: the GHSA is the axios project's own advisory, the CNA is GitHub (the same organization publishing the GHSA entry), and NVD carries GitHub's metric as Secondary rather than an independently authored one. The GHSA credits an external reporter (kobi-s), but the technical text and PoC are the project's, and no independent third-party analysis or reproduction was found. Fix and release facts rest on git object identity and npm tarball equality, not on advisory prose.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read lib/helpers/formDataToStream.js at v1.15.0 and confirm that value.type reaches the Content-Type header at line 27 without CR/LF filtering, while name/filename and string values are sanitized.
An independent reviewer must confirm that v1.15.0 is inside the advisory range and is the exact tag commit 772a4e54, and that the file judged is the snapshot file (blob f191e8cb).
An independent reviewer must verify fix commit 7587327 and release v1.15.1 from the git objects and the npm 1.15.1 tarball, including that the fixed file strips CR and LF from type.

An independent reviewer must assess whether the flaw is actually reachable through the public API for spec-compliant FormData, and whether the multipart body injection has plausible impact on a downstream parser.

An independent reviewer must decide whether the evidence is independent of the primary advisory source; the dossier records independent_of_primary=false because the GHSA, CNA and NVD metric all trace to GitHub, so evidence_independent may fail and keep the entry below promotion.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No JavaScript was executed and no HTTP request was made: the injection path is read from source and the fix tests, not reproduced against a live server.

Reachability requires the application to build a spec-compliant FormData from attacker-influenced Blob/File objects (for example a file relay or proxy) and post it with axios in Node.js; browser adapters and non-FormData bodies are unaffected.
Impact depends on the downstream multipart parser treating injected lines as per-part headers; the advisory argues this is common, but no independent parser-level demonstration was reviewed.

The advisory suggests value.name may have the same issue; at v1.15.0 name and filename already pass through escapeName, which percent-encodes CR, LF and quote, and the fix tests assert that escaping. Only value.type is treated as the promoted flaw.
The Node.js default require entry is dist/node/axios.cjs, a bundled build; the audit and tarball comparison cover lib/helpers/formDataToStream.js, and the bundle was not inspected.
Only v1.15.0 was analysed inside the range; earlier 1.x releases and the lower end of the range rest on the advisory and the invariant in the source.
The shallow git fetch prevents merge-base ancestry checks; v1.15.0 predates the fix commit by date and both objects were read by exact SHA.
The NVD record has no NVD-authored CVSS; severity and weakness rest on GitHub's Secondary data.
open_questions: Whether the bundled dist/node/axios.cjs in 1.15.0 contains the same unsanitized interpolation, which would matter for applications using the default require entry; not inspected.
Which downstream multipart parsers actually accept injected header lines as new part headers, which determines the realistic integrity impact.
Whether boundary-aware phantom field injection is practical, since the advisory notes it requires knowing the boundary.
Whether any independent third party analysed or reproduced the flaw; none was found, so evidence independence is expected to fail unless the reviewer finds one.
